name: Mattithiah
overview: Mattithiah was a male descendant of Nebo noted in the book of Ezra. He is specifically identified by his unique circumstance of having married a foreign wife, a detail that highlights the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenantal purity. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattithiah means "gift of YHWH," reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew proper name. This meaning underscores the biblical theme of God's provision and blessing, though the name itself is not indicated as being given directly by God in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Mattithiah was a descendant of Nebo, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Mattithiah's mention in Ezra 10:43 serves as a representative case of the post-exilic community's struggle to uphold the covenant by addressing intermarriage with foreign wives. His inclusion in the list of those who had married foreign women highlights the community's need for repentance and restoration in accordance with God's commands. Thus, Mattithiah's role, though brief, underscores the importance of faithfulness to God's covenant in the restoration period.
